profile.summary: HyenaDNA is a family of DNA language models that read very long stretches of genome one base at a time, up to 1 million bases in the largest model. It was pretrained on the human reference genome by predicting the next base, and it outputs per-base embeddings that can be fine-tuned for tasks such as finding regulatory elements or classifying species.

summary_quotes.text: HyenaDNA is a long-range genomic foundation model pretrained on context lengths of up to \***1 million tokens**\* at \***single nucleotide resolution**\*.
We pretrain using next token (nucleotide) prediction on the human reference genome (HG38).
including predicting regulatory elements, chromatin profiles, and species classification

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: HyenaDNA replaces attention with a stack of Hyena operators, which use input projections, implicit long convolutions and gating and scale sub-quadratically with sequence length. Each layer has a global receptive field. A single-character tokenizer with a vocabulary of the 4 nucleotides plus special tokens keeps single-base resolution. The model is causal: it is pretrained by next-nucleotide prediction on the human reference genome (HG38), and the inference script pads on the left for that reason.

quotes.text: HyenaDNA uses a simple stack of [Hyena](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.10866) operators, which are a subquadratic drop-in replacement for attention in Transformers.
by using modified input projections, implicit convolutions and gating, all subquadratic operations
We use a single character tokenizer with a primary vocab of 4 nucleotides (plus special tokens)
the implicit long convolution enables a **global receptive field** at each layer
padding_side='left', # since HyenaDNA is causal, we pad on the left

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The README lists seven pretrained checkpoints of different size and training sequence length, all trained on hg38: tiny-1k, tiny-1k-d256, tiny-16k-d128, small-32k, medium-160k, medium-450k and large-1m. Each exists as a weights-only repository for the original GitHub code and as a transformers-compatible copy with an -hf suffix; the model card says the two give identical outputs. A result should name the checkpoint, which interface was used, and the revision; this page read LongSafari/hyenadna-large-1m-seqlen-hf at revision 0a629abf. A Docker image with the exact Nucleotide Transformer benchmark settings from the paper is also provided.
sections.source_locator: README: Hugging Face pretrained weights; Dockerfile; model card: Links to all HuggingFace models; Hugging Face API response

quotes.text: There are different model sizes, and different training sequence lengths that they can handle up to. All pretrained on a single human reference genome (hg38).

There are also original weights-only versions of each model in the [LongSafari organization](https://huggingface.co/LongSafari), which are designed to be loaded with the original [github](https://github.com/HazyResearch/hyena-dna) repo. These models have identical outputs to the models in the collection above, just different interfaces.

We actually have a second Docker image, which has all the Nucleotide Transformer datasets, checkpoint, and exact commands and hyperparameter settings used to reproduce the best results in the HyenaDNA paper.
We pretrain using next token (nucleotide) prediction

strengths.text: Reads up to 1 million bases at single-base resolution in the largest checkpoint, without the k-mer or fixed tokenisers that the paper says lose single-nucleotide resolution.

quotes.text: pretrained on context lengths of up to \***1 million tokens**\* at \***single nucleotide resolution**\*
these methods rely on tokenizers or fixed k-mers to aggregate meaningful DNA units, losing single nucleotide resolution

strengths.text: Sizes run from tiny-1k to large-1m, and the model card suggests a GPU for five of the seven checkpoints: tiny-1k runs on a T4 for pretraining, fine-tuning and inference.
strengths.source_locator: model card: GPU requirements (suggested); README: checkpoint list

strengths.text: Weights are available both for the original training code and as transformers-compatible -hf copies with identical outputs, under permissive licences (BSD-3-Clause weights, Apache-2.0 code).

quotes.text: These models have identical outputs to the models in the collection above, just different interfaces.

limitations.text: Pretrained only on the human reference genome hg38; no checkpoints trained on other species or on population variation are listed.

quotes.text: All pretrained on a single human reference genome (hg38).

limitations.text: The model is causal and reads one direction. A bidirectional variant exists only for training from scratch on a downstream task, without masked language model pretraining.

run_guide.summary: Install the repository's dependencies at a pinned commit and run the standalone huggingface.py script, which downloads a pretrained checkpoint and prints the shape of the embeddings for a sample sequence.
prerequisites: conda and git. The README asks for Python 3.8+ and says the repository is developed with Pytorch 1.13 and CUDA 11.7.
git lfs: huggingface.py downloads the checkpoint by running git lfs install and git clone.
A GPU is used when available, otherwise the script falls back to CPU. The developers suggest a T4 for inference up to medium-450k and an A100-40GB for large-1m.
Code is Apache-2.0 and weights BSD-3-Clause. The weights are not gated.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/HazyResearch/hyena-dna.git && cd hyena-dna
git checkout --detach d553021b483b82980aa4b868b37ec2d4332e198a
steps.explanation: Clones the repository with its flash-attention submodule. The checkout line is added to pin the commit this page was written from.

steps.title: Create the environment and install PyTorch
steps.shell:
conda create -n hyena-dna python=3.8
conda activate hyena-dna
conda install pytorch==1.13.0 torchvision==0.14.0 torchaudio==0.13.0 pytorch-cuda=11.7 -c pytorch -c nvidia
steps.explanation: The README's create and install commands. The conda activate line is added so the install goes into the new environment.

quotes.text: conda install pytorch==1.13.0 torchvision==0.14.0 torchaudio==0.13.0 pytorch-cuda=11.7 -c pytorch -c nvidia

steps.title: Install requirements and Flash Attention
steps.shell:
pip install -r requirements.txt
git submodule update --init
cd flash-attention
git submodule update --init
pip install -e . --no-build-isolation
cd ..
steps.explanation: The README's dependency steps. Its 'cd hyena-dna' line is left out because the shell is already in the repository, and a final 'cd ..' is added to return to the repository root.

quotes.text: cd flash-attention git submodule update --init pip install -e . --no-build-isolation

steps.title: Run the inference example
steps.explanation: Downloads the small-32k checkpoint into ./checkpoints, tokenises a sample sequence of that length and runs a forward pass. To use another checkpoint, edit pretrained_model_name in the script.

quotes.text: # you only need to select which model to use here, we'll do the rest!

outputs: The script prints the device it uses, then the shape of the embedding tensor for the sample sequence.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The Flash Attention build can be slow; the README does not say whether huggingface.py needs it.
The script's sample sequence is a repeated ACTG pattern; replace it with your own sequence for real use.
